pages.note: Re-audited 2026-09-16 against published extension@4.1.19 and the merged Safari session commit 0508e40cd, which this page documents and which is unreleased as of 4.1.19. The previous record was written against 4.1.3 and described a page that no longer exists. Verified by running 4.1.19: every Safari identity flag on dev and build (--bundle-id, --app-name, --development-team, --macos-only defaulting to true, --force-regenerate, --safari-binary on dev only, --open on build only), the webkit-based alias in both -b enums, preview and start both refusing a Safari target with E_COMMAND_UNSUPPORTED_FOR_TARGET, and `logs --browser safari` resolving dist/extension-js/safari/logs.ndjson. The old 4.1.3 finding is gone: both commands now emit the documented code, and the page names that code once, on the preview row. Checked against the commit rather than run, because the rest needs macOS with Xcode and a live Safari: the twelve API namespaces match warn-gecko-unsupported-apis.ts exactly, content_scripts[].world is kept (DROP_CONTENT_SCRIPT_WORLD is false, and browsers-lib/messages.ts names Safari 18 as the reason), the pluginkit poll is 6 attempts 800ms apart, the xcodebuild tail is 50 lines and 8 KB, the scheme is the app name for a macOS-only project and `<App> (macOS)` otherwise, both PRODUCT_BUNDLE_IDENTIFIER entries are rewritten with .Extension on the extension target, the preserved signing settings are exactly DEVELOPMENT_TEAM, CODE_SIGN_STYLE and PROVISIONING_PROFILE_SPECIFIER, the derived id is dev.extensionjs.<sanitized app name> against the reverse-DNS validator the page describes, and SafariDevPlugin dispatches a control-bridge reload after each resync at the same granularity as Chromium. One finding, fixed here. The regeneration section described the v2 fingerprint, which is what 4.1.19 still writes but not what 0508e40cd writes, so the one section of the page pinned to the released CLI contradicted the commit the rest of the page is written against. Rewritten to the v4 shape (identity inputs, the top-level entries of dist/safari, the icons set, and the judged manifest surface) and marked with a TODO(version) comment naming 0508e40cd, matching the five markers the page already carries. No findings remain. Not re-measured and still carried from 0508e40cd: the roughly 4 second save-to-reload figure and everything else gated on macOS 26.5.2, Safari 26.5.2 and Xcode 26.6. Worth knowing for the next audit, and not a defect in this page: published 4.1.19 help still prints two claims this page corrected, the -b enum calling safari 'macOS only; no live reload' (already fixed at engine HEAD) and --development-team saying an ad-hoc build needs Develop, Allow Unsigned Extensions re-ticked on every launch, which is still present at engine HEAD and contradicts the measured page.

Every documented flag, default, and the one-shot contract were checked by running `extension logs --help` and `extension logs` with no session: the path dist/extension-js/chromium/logs.ndjson, the E_LOGS_NOT_FOUND envelope, and exit code 1 all matched exactly. Follow-mode/pretty-record claims need a live dev session and were not run.

Mostly conceptual. Checkable items verified: --polyfill exists on dev/build/start, one project produces separate dist/<browser> outputs (built dist/chromium and dist/firefox), Firefox uses background.scripts, and all seven cross-references resolve to real .mdx files.

Browser/engine names all appear in the dev --help enum (waterfox, librewolf, chromium-based, gecko-based, safari, webkit-based); framework rows agree with the pages they link to; CSS optional-dep rows agree with programs/develop/lib/optional-deps-contracts.ts; deno.jsonc scaffolding confirmed. The Safari-on-Windows/Linux row contradicts docs/browsers/safari.mdx and the CLI's own safariPackagingSkippedNonMac message.

Ran the tutorial end to end: `extension create github-search` then adding the page's root manifest.json and service_worker.js, then `extension build`. The scaffold is the javascript sidebar template rooted at src/, so both tutorial files are silently ignored and the built manifest has no omnibox key. The shown package.json also does not match what create emits.

Built the scratch project three ways to check the background contract: outputs background/service_worker.js and background/scripts.js confirmed; Firefox translated a plain background.service_worker into background.scripts:["background/service_worker.js"]; Chromium dropped the scripts key and kept service_worker when both were declared. Both template names (action, ai-chatgpt) and their screenshots exist.
Pure conceptual guidance about WebExtension messaging APIs with no Extension.js-specific behavior to exercise; the only checkable items were the three cross-references, which all resolve.

Template new-config-eslint is in the `extension create --help` catalog and exists in the examples repo; its screenshot exists at images/examples/new-config-eslint/screenshot.png; `deno add -D` is a real flag on deno 2.9.2; links to prettier and stylelint pages resolve.
Index page whose only checkable claims are its eleven cross-references, all of which resolve. The file ends on a bare '## Video walkthrough' heading with no video under it.

The only locally checkable claim is `npx extension build --browser edge --zip`, and both flags exist per `build --help`. Partner Center portal layout, API-key 72-day expiry, and the retired Azure AD model need a Partner Center account and are unverifiable here; the EDGE_* env names are the page's own CI convention, consistent with docs/publishing/index.mdx which says you set them in your own CI.
Conceptual pre-release checklist with no Extension.js commands, flags, or output paths to exercise; both cross-references resolve to real pages.
